issues.detail: Hebrew 'בֶן קָשֶׁת' means 'son of the bow' (i.e., an archer), not '弓的兒子' (son of the bow) — the Chinese rendering is literal but ambiguous; however, the main issue is 'לְקַשׁ נֶהְפְּכוּ לוֹ אַבְנֵי קָלַע' — the Hebrew says 'the stones of the sling were turned to chaff for him' (i.e., sling stones became like chaff/straw to him), but the Chinese says '禾稈殘茬對他變成了石塊' (stubble/straw became stones for him), reversing the direction of the transformation. The Hebrew states that sling stones became chaff, not that chaff became stones.
